title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
claim: A plain transformer can denoise raw geometry patches directly, conditioned on frozen pretrained image features, with no tokenizer or hybrid modules.
layout: Single column, top-to-bottom; inputs on top, model block in middle, output below; snowflake/fire icons
description: A vertical pipeline. At the top, a noisy point map (a grid-patched, noise-corrupted RGB-coded 3D map) sits on the left. An input photo of a tabletop scene (teapot, glass bottle, tuna can, remote) sits on the right. Gray arrows labeled Patchify and DINOv3 lead down to two rows of square tokens: noisy point tokens above and DINOv3 feature tokens below, with ellipsis dots between the left and right groups. A large gray rounded container, marked with a fire icon for trainable, holds three light-blue bars: Linear Embed, Transformer Block (×L), and Linear Predict. DINOv3 carries a snowflake icon for frozen. Below the container are clean denoised point tokens in green-to-purple tones. An Unpatchify arrow leads to the final gridded Clean Point Map at the bottom. Saturated token colors draw the eye first.
caption: PointDiT. A minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer operating directly on raw point map patches, conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. The 3D point map (H × W × 3) is visualized as an RGB image, with color encoding the spatial (X, Y, Z) coordinates.
abstract: State-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction methods often rely on complex hybrid architectures and loss functions, or compress geometry into latent spaces in order to leverage pre-trained latent diffusion models. In this work, we show that such architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary. We introduce a minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer, built on a plain ViT, that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches and is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. Unlike existing latent diffusion approaches, we train our diffusion backbone entirely from scratch, eliminating the need for point map tokenizers. Despite its simplicity, our approach surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while remaining significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives. Notably, it produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions, such as transparent objects.
